titleEn: The Glory of Kings — The Ascension and the Second Coming in the Prophets (ch. 111)
part: ch. 111 — the ascension and the second coming in the prophets
about: Chapter 111 turns the author's proof from the prophets to Christ's ascension and return. David (Psalms 68, 24, 62, 21 and 18), Amos, Zechariah (14:4–5) and Daniel (7:13–14) are quoted in the usual frame 'and as X prophesied, he said', with Psalm 24's 'who is this king of glory?' at the centre. The author then says that nothing happened without the prophets, who prophesied in deed as well as word, and gives Abraham's descent into Egypt and return in wealth as the type of Christ's descent and ascent. Two units (47 and 48 words) hold several quotations with no ፤ and stay whole. The quotations are the author's own wording, so notes name a source only where clear and flag doubtful words with (?). Dillmann's lexicon was not available for this draft.

sentences.i: Chapter 111: Concerning his ascension and his second coming
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ፻፲፩ is the numeral 111 (፻ hundred, ፲ ten, ፩ one). በእንተ 'concerning' takes ዕርገቱ, ዕርገት 'ascension' (from ዐረገ 'go up') with -ሁ 'his' (ዕርገት + ሁ is written ዕርገቱ). ወዳግም ምጽአቱ is 'and second coming his': ዳግም 'second, again' and ምጽአት 'coming' (from መጽአ 'come') with -ሁ, in apposition, so 'and his second coming'. The chapter is another catena of prophecies, each opened by ወበከመ ተነበየ X ወይቤ 'and as X prophesied, he said', as in the previous part.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበዩ ፡ ነቢያት ፡ ኵሎሙ ፡ ወአበው ፡ ቀደምት ፡ ብዙኀ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዕርገቱ ፡ ወዳግም ፡ ምጽአቱ ፡ ይኰንን ፡ ሕያዋነ ፡ ወሙታነ ፡ ወዳዊትኒ ፡ ይቤ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዕርገቱ ፡ ዐረገ ፡ ውስተ ፡ አርያም ፡ ፄዊወከ ፡ ፄዋ ፡ ወወህብከ ፡ ጸጋከ ፡ ለእጓለ ፡ እመሕያው ፤
sentences.l: And-as they-prophesied prophets all and-fathers ancient much concerning ascension-his and-second coming-his, he-will-judge living and-dead; and-David-too said concerning ascension-his: 'He-ascended into height; you-took-captive captivity(?), and-you-gave grace-your to-son-of man;
sentences.i: As all the prophets and the fathers of old prophesied at length(?) about his ascension and his second coming, when he will judge the living and the dead, so David also spoke about his ascension: 'He went up on high; you took captivity captive, and gave your gift to the sons of men;
sentences.n: The frame is double: ወበከመ ተነበዩ 'and as they prophesied' (tä-stem perfect of ነበየ, 3mp) opens a comparison, and ወዳዊትኒ ይቤ 'and David too said' (ዳዊት + emphatic -ኒ) is the matching clause. ነቢያት ኵሎሙ 'all the prophets' (ኵሎሙ is ኵሉ + -ሙ, 'all of them'); አበው ቀደምት 'the early fathers'; ብዙኀ is the accusative form 'much', which I take as an adverb (?). ይኰንን is the imperfect of ኰነነ 'judge' (3ms): 'he will judge', or 'who will judge'; ሕያዋነ ወሙታነ 'living and dead' are accusatives (-ነ). Then Psalm 68:18 (67:19 in the Greek numbering), quoted of the ascension as in Ephesians 4:8. ዐረገ 'he went up'; አርያም 'the height, the heights' (a Geʿez word for heaven's height); ፄዊወከ ፄዋ is a figura etymologica, 'you took captive captivity' (the root is ፄወወ, 'take captive', and ፄዋ the noun 'captivity'; I take it so, with Dillmann not available (?)). ወህብከ 'you gave'; ጸጋ 'grace, gift' with -ከ 'your'; ለእጓለ እመሕያው, literally 'to the offspring of the son of man', is the usual Geʿez 'to mankind' (እጓለ እመሕያው is 'son of man', so 'the sons of men' in English). The unit ends at ፤ with the quotation still open.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ይቤ ፡ እግዚአብሔር ፡ ወፂእየ ፡ እገብእ ፡ ወእትመየጥ ፡ እንተ ፡ ቀላየ ፡ ባሕር ፤
sentences.l: And-again said God: 'And-having-gone-out I-will-return, and-I-will-turn-back, which(?) depths-of sea;
sentences.i: And again God said: 'Having gone out, I will return, and turn back(?) from the depths of the sea;
sentences.n: Psalm 68:22 (67:23 in the Greek numbering), 'I will bring back from the depths of the sea', but the Geʿez has the speaker himself returning. ፂእየ is a gerund, 'having gone out' (ወጽአ 'go out'), with the first-person ending -የ; እገብእ 'I will return' (ገብአ) and እትመየጥ 'I will turn back' (tä-stem of መየጠ 'turn'). እንተ is the feminine relative pronoun 'which', which fits poorly before ቀላየ ባሕር; I take it as standing for 'from, to' (?), and ቀላየ, the construct state of ቀላይ, 'the depths of' (?), a reading from the psalm's sense. ባሕር 'sea'. The unit ends at ፤.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ዘምሩ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ዘዐርገ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሰማይ ፤
sentences.l: And-again said: 'Sing to-God, who-ascended into heaven;
sentences.i: And again he said: 'Sing to God, who went up into heaven;
sentences.n: Psalm 68:32–33 (67:33–34 in the Greek numbering). ዘምሩ is the imperative plural of ዘመረ 'sing, praise with song'; ለእግዚኣብሔር 'to God'; ዘዐርገ 'who ascended' (relative ዘ- + perfect). ሰማይ 'heaven'. The quotation runs on into the next unit.

sentences.i: To the heaven that lies toward the east.'
sentences.n: Psalm 68:33 has 'to him who rides on the heaven of heavens toward the east', and here only 'heaven' remains. ዘመንገለ ጽባሕ is ዘ- 'of, that (is)' + መንገለ 'toward' + ጽባሕ 'east, morning': 'that is toward the east'. The ascension is placed toward the east, where Zechariah's Mount of Olives (below) lies. The source prints this short unit as a separate sentence and I keep it so.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ አሞጽ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ መሲሕ ፡ ዘይገብር ፡ ጊዜ ፡ በጽሐ ፡ ወይትሌዐል ፡ እምድር ፡ ውስተ ፡ አርያም ፤
sentences.l: And-as prophesied Amos prophet and-said: 'Messiah, who does(?) time: has-arrived(?), and-he-will-be-exalted from-earth to height;
sentences.i: And as the prophet Amos prophesied, he said: 'The Messiah, who acts(?) in time(?): it has come, and he will be lifted up from the earth to the height;
sentences.n: I cannot match these words to a verse of Amos; Amos 9:6 ('he who builds his ascents in the heavens') and Amos 4:13 are the nearest, so this may be a paraphrase (?). መሲሕ 'Messiah'. The clause ዘይገብር ጊዜ በጽሐ is hard: ዘይገብር is 'who does, who makes' (ዘ- + imperfect of ገብረ), ጊዜ 'time', በጽሐ 'has arrived' (3ms); I read 'the Messiah who acts: the time has come' with the two parts loosely joined (?), and I keep it uncertain. ይትሌዐል 'he will be exalted' (tä-stem of ልዕለ, 'be high'); እምድር is እም- 'from' + ምድር 'earth'; ውስተ አርያም 'into the height'. The unit ends at ፤.

sentences.t: ወእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ስሙ ፡ ዘኵሎ ፡ ይመልክ ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ተለዐልከ ፡ እግዚኦ ፡ በኀይልከ ፡ ንሴብሕ ፡ ወንዜምር ፡ ለጽንዕከ ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዘካርያስ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ወይቀውማ ፡ እገሪሁ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ደብረ ፡ ዘይት ፡ ጽባሒሃ ፡ ለኢየሩሳሌም ፡ ወተጽዕነ ፡ ላዕለ ፡ ኪሩቤል ፡ ወሰረረ ፡ በክነፈ ፡ ነፋስ ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ አርኅዉ ፡ ኆኃተ ፡ መኳንንት ፡ ወይትረኀዋ ፡ ኆኃት ፡ እለ ፡ እምፍጥረት ፡ ወይባእ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ስብሐት ፤
sentences.l: And-God name-his, who-all he-rules; and-as prophesied David prophet and-said: 'You-were-exalted, O-Lord, in-your-might; we-praise and-we-sing to-your-strength; and-as prophesied Zechariah prophet and-said: 'And-will-stand feet-his upon mountain-of olive, east-of-her, of-Jerusalem; and-he-rode upon cherubim, and-sped(?) on-wing-of wind; and-as said David: 'Open gates-of rulers, and-let-be-opened gates which from-creation, and-let-enter king-of glory;
sentences.i: 'And God is his name, who rules over all.' And as the prophet David prophesied, he said: 'You were exalted, Lord, in your might; we will praise and sing of your strength.' And as the prophet Zechariah prophesied, he said: 'His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem; and he rode on the cherubim, and sped(?) on the wing of the wind.' And as David said: 'Open, you rulers, your gates, and let the gates that are from creation be opened, and let the king of glory enter;
sentences.n: The longest unit of the part: 47 words, with no ፤ inside it, so by the rule it stays whole and I do not cut it, though it holds five quotations in a row. The first, ወእግዚኣብሔር ስሙ ዘኵሎ ይመልክ, finishes the Amos saying of the previous unit, 'and God is his name, who rules all' (ዘ- + imperfect of መለከ 'rule'); this is close to Amos 4:13 and 9:6 ('the Lord is his name'), so the closing quotation mark in the English is placed there. Then Psalm 21:13 (20:13 in the Greek numbering): ተለዐልከ 'you were exalted' (perfect, 2ms), በኀይልከ 'in your might', ንሴብሕ ወንዜምር 'let us / we will praise and sing' (1cp), ለጽንዕከ 'to / of your strength'. Then Zechariah 14:4: ወይቀውማ 'and will stand' (3fp imperfect, agreeing with እገሪሁ 'his feet'; I read the ending as a feminine plural (?)), እገሪሁ 'his feet', ደብረ ዘይት 'the Mount of Olives' (ደብር 'mountain' in construct, ዘይት 'olive'), ጽባሒሃ ለኢየሩሳሌም 'its east, Jerusalem's' (ጽባሒ + -ሃ 'her', then ለ- names the possessor). Then, without a new frame, Psalm 18:10 (17:11): ወተጽዕነ 'and he rode' (tä-stem, 'was borne, rode'), ኪሩቤል 'cherubim', ወሰረረ 'and he sped' is uncertain (?), በክነፈ ነፋስ 'on the wing of the wind' (ክነፍ construct before ነፋስ). Then Psalm 24:7–9 (23:7–9): አርኅዉ 'open!' (imperative pl), ኆኃተ መኳንንት 'the gates of the rulers' (Psalm 24 has 'lift up your heads, O gates'), ወይትረኀዋ 'and let them be opened' (jussive, fem. pl.), ኆኃት እለ እምፍጥረት 'the gates that are from creation' (እለ plural relative, እም- 'from', ፍጥረት 'creation'; the Greek has 'eternal gates'), ወይባእ 'and let him enter' (jussive of ቦአ), ንጉሠ ስብሐት 'the king of glory' (ንጉሥ in construct state, ንጉሠ, before ስብሐት 'glory'). Two quotations open here that the source never closes; the English marks only the ones the grammar shows.

sentences.t: መኑ ፡ ውእ ፡ ቱ ፡ ዝንቱ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ስብሐት ፤
sentences.i: Who is he, this king of glory?
sentences.n: Psalm 24:8 (23:8). The source prints ውእ ፡ ቱ with a wordspace inside the word, 'ውእ ቱ'; this is a printing oddity, and the word is ውእቱ 'he, it is' (3ms pronoun), kept as printed in the Geʿez. መኑ 'who?'; ዝንቱ 'this' (masculine); ንጉሠ ስብሐት is the construct state, 'king of glory' (ንጉሠ, the construct state of ንጉሥ 'king', before ስብሐት 'glory'). The unit ends at ፤ because the answer follows.

sentences.t: እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ኀያል ፡ ወጽኑዕ ፡ እግዚአብሔር ፡ ኀያል ፡ በውስተ ፡ ፀብእ ፤
sentences.l: The-Lord strong and-mighty, the-Lord strong in-the-midst-of battle;
sentences.i: The Lord, strong and mighty, the Lord, strong in battle;
sentences.n: Psalm 24:8 (23:8), the first answer. ኀያል 'strong, mighty' and ጽኑዕ 'firm, mighty'; the second ኀያል is repeated for emphasis. በውስተ ፀብእ is በ- 'in' + ውስተ 'into, in the midst of' + ፀብእ 'battle, war'. Note the two spellings of 'God' in this chapter: እግዚአብሔር and እግዚኣብሔር, both 'the Lord God', and I do not mark them as different.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ አጠየቀ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ አርኅዉ ፡ ኆኃተ ፡ መኳንንት ፡ ወይትረኀዋ ፡ ኆኃት ፡ እለ ፡ እምፍጥረት ፡ ወይባእ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ስብሐት ፤
sentences.l: And-again he-asked and-said: 'Open gates-of rulers, and-let-be-opened gates which from-creation, and-let-enter king-of glory;
sentences.i: And again he asked, and said: 'Open, you rulers, your gates, and let the gates that are from creation be opened, and let the king of glory enter;
sentences.n: Psalm 24:9 (23:9), the second challenge, the same words as in the long unit above. አጠየቀ 'he asked' (አጠየቀ I take as 'he asked, inquired', from context (?)). ወካዕበ 'and again'. The rest repeats the earlier quotation word for word, with the same notes.

sentences.i: Who is he, this king of glory?
sentences.n: Psalm 24:10 (23:10), repeated. Here ውእቱ is printed whole, unlike the earlier ውእ ቱ.

sentences.t: እግዚአብሔር ፡ አምላከ ፡ ኀያላን ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ዝንቱ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ስብሐት ።
sentences.l: The-Lord God-of the-mighty is-he, this king-of glory.
sentences.i: The Lord, the God of the mighty, he is this king of glory.
sentences.n: Psalm 24:10 (23:10). The Greek and Hebrew have 'Lord of hosts', here the Geʿez has አምላከ ኀያላን 'God of the mighty (ones)' (አምላክ construct before ኀያላን, plural of ኀያል). The pronoun ውእቱ ዝንቱ 'he, this one' sums up. The ። closes the long run of quotations on the ascension.

sentences.t: ወበእንተ ፡ ምጽአቱ ፡ ዳግመ ፡ ይኴንን ፡ ሕያዋነ ፡ ወሙታነ ፡ ዘሎቱ ፡ ስብሐት ፡ ለዓለመ ፡ ዓለም ፡ አሜን ፤
sentences.l: And-concerning coming-his again he-will-judge living and-dead, to-whom glory for-age-of age, Amen;
sentences.i: And concerning his coming again, when he will judge the living and the dead, to whom be glory for ever and ever, Amen;
sentences.n: The author turns from the ascension to the return. ወበእንተ 'and concerning' (ወ- + በእንተ); ዳግመ is the accusative of ዳግም 'again'; ይኴንን 'he will judge' is the same verb as ይኰንን in unit 1, in a variant spelling of the vowel (ኰ and ኴ) that I leave as printed. ዘሎቱ ስብሐት 'to whom (is) glory' (ዘ- 'who' + ሎቱ 'to him'). ለዓለመ ዓለም 'for ever and ever', literally 'to the age of the age' (the construct ዓለመ), an ending that recurs; አሜን 'amen'. The unit ends at ፤.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዘካርያስ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ውእተ ፡ አሚረ ፡ ይመጽእ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ አምላኪየ ፡ ወኵሎሙ ፡ ቅዱሳኒሁ ፡ ምስሌሁ ።
sentences.l: And-as prophesied Zechariah prophet: 'In-that day he-will-come the-Lord my-God, and-all-of-them his-saints with-him.'
sentences.i: And as the prophet Zechariah prophesied: 'On that day the Lord my God will come, and all his holy ones with him.'
sentences.n: Zechariah 14:5, 'the Lord my God will come, and all the holy ones with him'. ውእተ አሚረ 'on that day' (a fixed accusative phrase of time: ውእተ 'that' and አሚር 'day'). ይመጽእ 'he will come' (imperfect of መጽአ). አምላኪየ 'my God' (አምላክ + -የ, with the vowel -ኪ as the construct-state form before the suffix); ቅዱሳኒሁ 'his saints' (plural of ቅዱስ + -ሁ), ወኵሎሙ 'and all of them'; ምስሌሁ 'with him' (ምስል + -ሁ). The author takes the 'holy ones' as the angels and the saints at the judgement.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ምዕረ ፡ ነበበ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወዘንተ ፡ ክመ ፡ ሰማዕኩ ፤
sentences.l: And-as prophesied David prophet and-said: 'Once spoke God, and-this too(?) I-heard;
sentences.i: And as the prophet David prophesied, he said: 'God has spoken once, and this too(?) I have heard;
sentences.n: Psalm 62:11 (61:12 in the Greek numbering): 'God has spoken once; these two things I have heard'. ምዕረ 'once'; ነበበ 'he spoke' (perfect of ነበበ, which is not the same verb as ተነበየ 'prophesied'); ወዘንተ is ወ- + ዘንተ, 'and this' (the accusative of ዝንቱ). The word ክመ I read as 'also, too' (?); the Greek has 'two things', so it may rather be a form meaning 'two' (?). ሰማዕኩ 'I heard' (perfect, 1cs). The unit ends at ፤.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ዘእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ሣህል ፡ ወዚአከ ፡ እግዚኦ ፡ ኀይል ፡ እስመ ፡ አንተ ፡ ትፈድዮ ፡ ለኵሉ ፡ በከመ ፡ ምግባሩ ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዳንኤል ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ርኢኩ ፡ በራእየ ፡ ሌሊት ፡ ወናሁ ፡ መጽአ ፡ ከመ ፡ ወልደ ፡ እጓለ ፡ እመሕያው ፡ ኀበ ፡ ብሉየ ፡ መዋዕል ፡ ወተውህበ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ምኵናን ፡ ወክብር ፡ ወመንግሥት ፡ ወኵሎሙ ፡ አሕዛብ ፡ ወነገድ ፡ ወበሓውርት ፡ ተቀንዩ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ወምኵናኑኒ ፡ ዘአልቦ ፡ ማኅለቅተ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለመ ፡ ዓለም ፡ አሜን ፨
sentences.l: for of-the-Lord mercy, and-yours, O-Lord, power; for you you-repay to-all according-to-work-his; and-as prophesied Daniel prophet and-said: 'I-saw in-vision-of night, and-behold he-came like son-of man to the-aged-of days; and-was-given to-him authority and-honour and-kingdom, and-all peoples and-tribe and-in-goings(?) served to-him; and-authority-his-too, which has-not end, until for-age-of age, Amen.
sentences.i: for mercy is the Lord's, and yours, Lord, is power; for you repay everyone according to his work.' And as the prophet Daniel prophesied, he said: 'I saw in a vision of the night, and behold, one like a son of man came to the Ancient of Days; and authority and honour and kingdom were given to him, and all peoples and tribes and the ...(?) served him; and his authority has no end, for ever and ever, Amen.
sentences.n: Another long unit: 48 words, ending at ፨ with no ፤ inside, so it stays whole. It finishes Psalm 62:12 (61:13) and then quotes Daniel 7:13–14, the 'one like a son of man'. እስመ 'for'; ዘእግዚኣብሔር ሣህል 'of the Lord (is) mercy' (ዘ- 'of' marks the possessor, put first); ወዚአከ 'and yours' (ዚአ + -ከ); ትፈድዮ 'you repay' (imperfect of ፈደየ 'repay, requite'), ለኵሉ 'to all', በከመ ምግባሩ 'according to his work' (በከመ 'according as'; ምግባር + -ሁ). Daniel: ርኢኩ 'I saw'; ራእይ 'vision'; ወናሁ 'and behold'; ከመ ወልደ እጓለ እመሕያው 'like the son of man' (the accusative after ከመ; the Geʿez doubles the 'son of man' phrase); ብሉየ መዋዕል 'the aged of days', the 'Ancient of Days'; ተውህበ ሎቱ 'was given to him'; ምኵናን 'authority' (also 'judgment'), ክብር 'honour', መንግሥት 'kingdom'. ነገድ 'tribe'. ወበሓውርት is uncertain: ሓውርት (from ሐወረ 'go') would be 'goings, journeys', but Daniel has 'languages' here, so the word, or the whole phrase, may be corrupt (?). ተቀንዩ 'they served' (tä-stem of ቀነየ, 'serve, be subject'). ወምኵናኑኒ 'and his authority too', ዘአልቦ ማኅለቅተ 'which has no end' (ማኅለቅት 'end' in the accusative after አልቦ). እስከ ለዓለመ ዓለም 'until for ever and ever'. The ፨ is the stop that closes the quotations and turns the author's own argument.

sentences.t: ወኵሎሙ ፡ ነቢያት ፡ ተነበዩ ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ዘኮነ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ትንቢተ ፡ ነቢያት ፡ ወኵሉ ፡ ነገሩ ፡ ዘኮነ ፡ ወዘይከውን ፡ ዘተገብረ ፡ ወዘይትገበር ፡ ዘቀዳሚ ፡ ወዘደኃሪ ፡ ወእስከ ፡ ዳግም ፡ ምጽአቱ ፤
sentences.l: And-all prophets prophesied, and-there-is-not what happened without prophecy-of prophets; and-all matters-his, what happened and-what will-be, what was-done and-what is-done, of-the-first and-of-the-last, and until second coming-his;
sentences.i: All the prophets prophesied, and nothing has happened without the prophecy of the prophets; and all his matters, what has happened and what will be, what was done and what is done, from the first and from the last, and up to his second coming;
sentences.n: The author's comment on the whole catena. ወአልቦ ዘኮነ ዘእንበለ ትንቢተ ነቢያት 'there is nothing that happened without the prophecy of the prophets': አልቦ 'there is not', ዘኮነ 'that was, happened' (ዘ- + perfect of ኮነ), ዘእንበለ 'without' (ዘ- + እንበለ), ትንቢተ the construct of ትንቢት 'prophecy'. Then four pairs, each joined by ወዘ-: ዘኮነ ወዘይከውን 'what has been and what will be' (perfect and imperfect of ኮነ), ዘተገብረ ወዘይትገበር 'what was done and what is done' (passive tä-stem of ገብረ, perfect and imperfect), ዘቀዳሚ ወዘደኃሪ 'of the first and of the last' (ቀዳሚ 'first', ደኃሪ 'last'), the whole 'from beginning to end'. ወእስከ ዳግም ምጽአቱ 'and until his second coming' (እስከ 'until'). The unit ends at ፤.

sentences.t: ወአኮ ፡ በቃል ፡ ባሕቲቱ ፡ ዘተነበዩ ፡ ወዘተናገሩ ፡ አላ ፡ በሥጋሆሙኒ ፡ አርአዩ ፡ ዘምስለ ፡ ትንቢት ፡ ወኮነ ፡ ረኃብ ፡ ምድረ ፡ ኮናአን ፡ ወወረደ ፡ አቡነ ፡ አብርሃም ፡ ግብጸ ፡ ወገብአ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ብዙኅ ፡ ብዕል ፡ ወክብር ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ጥልቀት ፤
sentences.l: And-not by-word alone, what they-prophesied and-what they-spoke, but in-bodies-their-too they-showed what with prophecy; and-was famine land-of Canaan, and-went-down our-father Abraham Egypt-ward, and-returned with much wealth and-honour, without loss(?);
sentences.i: And it was not by word alone that they prophesied and spoke, but they showed what goes with prophecy in their own bodies too: there was a famine in the land of Canaan, and our father Abraham went down into Egypt, and came back with great wealth and honour, without loss(?);
sentences.n: Now the prophets are said to have prophesied in deed as well as word, and the author's example is Abraham in Genesis 12:10–13:2 (famine, the descent into Egypt, the return rich). ወአኮ is ወ- + አኮ 'and not' (negating the phrase that follows); በቃል ባሕቲቱ 'by word alone' (ባሕቲቱ 'alone', ባሕቲት + -ሁ); ዘተነበዩ ወዘተናገሩ 'what they prophesied and what they spoke' (ተናገረ 'speak'), with ዘ- giving a relative sense; አላ 'but'; በሥጋሆሙኒ 'in their bodies too' (ሥጋ 'flesh' + -ሆሙ 'their' + -ኒ); አርአዩ 'they showed' (causative of ርእየ); ዘምስለ ትንቢት 'what is with prophecy', or 'what accompanies prophecy'. ኮነ ረኃብ 'there was a famine' (ኮነ 'was', ረኃብ 'hunger'); ምድረ ኮናአን 'the land of Canaan' (ምድር construct, ኮናአን Canaan). ወረደ 'went down'; አቡነ አብርሃም 'our father Abraham'; ግብጸ 'Egypt', accusative (ግብጽ), so 'went down to Egypt'. ገብአ 'returned'; ምስለ ብዙኅ ብዕል ወክብር 'with much wealth and honour'. ዘእንበለ ጥልቀት 'without' + ጥልቀት; I take ጥልቀት as 'harm, loss' (?), and Dillmann was not available. The unit ends at ፤.

sentences.t: ወከማሁ ፡ ወረደ ፡ መድኀኒነ ፡ ወአድኀነ ፡ ቤተ ፡ ክርስቲያኑ ፡ ማኅበረ ፡ አሕዛብ ፡ ወዐርገ ፡ ነሢኦ ፡ ክብረ ፡ ወስብሐተ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-likewise went-down our-saviour and-saved house-of his-Christian, assembly-of nations; and-ascended, taking glory and-praise. ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.i: And likewise our Saviour went down and saved his church, the assembly of the nations; and he ascended, taking glory and praise.
sentences.n: The type is drawn: as Abraham went down to Egypt and came back in wealth, so Christ went down and rose again in glory. ወከማሁ 'and likewise' (ከማሁ 'thus, so'); ወረደ 'went down'; መድኀኒነ 'our saviour' (መድኀኒ + -ነ); ወአድኀነ 'and saved' (causative of ድኅነ, 'be saved'); ቤተ ክርስቲያኑ 'his church', literally 'the house of his Christians' (ቤተ construct, ክርስቲያን + -ሁ), glossed by ማኅበረ አሕዛብ 'the assembly of nations' (ማኅበር construct, 'gathering'); ወዐርገ 'and he ascended'; ነሢኦ is the gerund of ነሥአ 'take', 'taking'; ክብረ ወስብሐተ 'glory and praise' (accusatives). The unit ends with ፨ and the run of six ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ is kept attached to it as printed, the mark of the end of the chapter and of the section on the prophets of the ascension.
